documents.title: Guidance on the Use of Generative AI and Large Language Model Tools
documents.stance_why: The memo aims "to encourage the responsible use" of GenAI and sets four principles (disclosure, data protection, content responsibility, honor code), but it sets no default ban or permission for coursework; it defers to "the course instructor" and "course requirements". With no stance of its own for courses, it delegates. Coder B coded permit; the memo states no permission or ban for coursework itself and defers to 'the course instructor', so delegates.
documents.summary: A short 2023 Provost and COO memo giving interim, institute-wide guidance on GenAI. It supports responsible experimentation and asks for disclosure, protection of sensitive data, verification of output, and compliance with the honor code, leaving course-level rules to instructors. It says the guidance will change.

units.why: The opening states the purpose: "to encourage the responsible use of generative artificial intelligence". It is a university-level framing of scope and purpose, so P56 (institution framework) fits, with actor all and phase general; it informs rather than binds.
units.resolution_why: A coded P56/informs, B coded P02/should. The sentence is the memo's statement of purpose and scope ('We write to provide initial guidance to encourage the responsible use ... in research, education, and administrative work'); it addresses no one with a duty, so informs, and it sets scope rather than the default rule (that is the next sentence, coded P02). Final P56, informs.
